info.name: CampusConnect Auth Service
info.description:
Complete Postman collection for the CampusConnect JWT Authentication Service (Experiment 8).

Stack: Python · Flask · PyJWT · Werkzeug · Flask-CORS
Base URL: http://127.0.0.1:5050

⚠️  DISCLAIMER: This experiment demonstrates JWT authentication concepts only.
    It does NOT implement a complete OAuth2 authorization server.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🚀  HOW TO RUN:
  1. cd auth_service
  2. Copy .env.example to .env and set JWT_SECRET
  3. pip install -r requirements.txt
  4. python app.py

🔁  RECOMMENDED TESTING ORDER:
  1.  Register Student
  2.  Register Admin
  3.  Login (student) → copy token to collection variable {{student_token}}
  4.  Login (admin)   → copy token to collection variable {{admin_token}}
  5.  Dashboard — Valid Token (student)
  6.  Dashboard — No Token
  7.  Dashboard — Invalid Token
  8.  Admin Events — Student Token (403)
  9.  Admin Events — Admin Token (200)
  10. Health Check
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

request.description:
Registers a new CampusConnect student account.

Expected Response: 201 Created
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Account created successfully. Welcome to CampusConnect, Sophia Patel!",
  "user": {
    "id": "<uuid>",
    "name": "Sophia Patel",
    "email": "sophia.patel@campusconnect.edu",
    "role": "student",
    "created_at": "..."
  }
}

⚠️  Note: password and password_hash are NEVER returned in any response.

Logs in the registered student and returns a signed JWT token.

Expected Response: 200 OK
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Login successful.",
  "token": "eyJ...<JWT>",
  "expires_at": "...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "user": {
    "id": "<uuid>",
    "name": "Sophia Patel",
    "email": "sophia.patel@campusconnect.edu",
    "role": "student",
    "created_at": "..."
  }
}

📋  AFTER RUNNING: Copy the 'token' value and paste it into the
    collection variable 'student_token'.

Logs in the registered admin and returns a signed JWT token with role='admin'.

Expected Response: 200 OK with token.

📋  AFTER RUNNING: Copy the 'token' value and paste it into the
    collection variable 'admin_token'.

Attempts login with correct email but wrong password.

Expected Response: 401 Unauthorized
{
  "success": false,
  "error": "Invalid email or password. Please check your credentials."
}

🔒 Note: The error message is intentionally generic — it does not reveal whether
   the email exists, preventing user enumeration attacks.

Attempts login with an email that was never registered.

Expected Response: 401 Unauthorized (same generic message as wrong password
to prevent user enumeration).

request.description:
Accesses the dashboard with a valid admin JWT token. Admin gets expanded permitted_actions.

Prerequisite: Run 'Login Admin' first and set {{admin_token}}.

Expected Response: 200 OK with role='admin' and extended permitted_actions.

Sends a JWT token with an expired timestamp. The service validates expiry and rejects it.

Expected Response: 401 Unauthorized
{
  "success": false,
  "error": "Token has expired. Please log in again." or "Invalid token: ..."
}

💡 Tip: To test with a truly expired token, set JWT_EXPIRY_HOURS=0 in .env
    (or a very small value), login, wait, then call this endpoint.

Sends the token WITHOUT the 'Bearer ' prefix.

Expected Response: 401 Unauthorized — Authorization header missing or malformed.

header.description: Valid student token — but this endpoint requires admin role

request.description:
Uses a perfectly valid student JWT token to access an admin-only endpoint.

Prerequisite: Set {{student_token}} from 'Login Student'.

Expected Response: 403 Forbidden
{
  "success": false,
  "error": "Access denied. This endpoint requires administrator privileges. Students are not authorised to access event management."
}

🔑 Key concept: The token IS valid (not expired, not tampered), but the user's
   ROLE does not permit access. This is role-based authorization.

header.description: Valid admin token — grants access to the admin events panel

request.description:
Accesses admin endpoint with no Authorization header at all.

Expected Response: 401 Unauthorized — Missing token error (auth check runs before role check).

Sends a malformed token to the admin endpoint.

Expected Response: 401 Unauthorized — Invalid token error.

Verifies the Flask auth service is running. No authentication required.

Expected Response: 200 OK
{
  "status": "ok",
  "service": "CampusConnect Auth Service",
  "experiment": "Experiment 8 — JWT Authentication",
  "registered_users": <count>
}
